---
title: "Before Lesson 1"
---

Install Sonic Pi from [sonic-pi.net](https://sonic-pi.net/). Version 4 or later.
The download page covers macOS, Windows, Linux, and Raspberry Pi, and the
installer is the whole setup.

Open it, type this into the first buffer, and press **Run**.

```ruby
play 60
```

If you hear a note, you are ready.

Headphones or decent speakers will do more for your progress than any other
purchase, because half of this course is hearing small differences. Laptop
speakers reproduce almost nothing below about 200 Hz, which is most of Part 1
and every bass line in Part 10.

## The window

Three areas matter. The **buffers** hold your code, and there are ten of them,
which is more useful than it sounds once you are running several voices. The
**log** on the right prints every note as it plays, and it is the first place to
look when something sounds wrong. The **help** pane at the bottom documents every
synth, sample, and function, and it is faster than searching the web.

Two shortcuts worth learning now: `Cmd-R` or `Alt-R` runs the buffer, and
`Cmd-.` or `Alt-.` stops everything.

## A first sound

Paste this in and run it. You are not expected to understand it yet. It is here
so you know what the destination sounds like.

```{.ruby audio="setup-1.mp3"}
# Four bars that already sound like music.
# Every construct here is explained by the end of Part 3.

use_bpm 96
use_synth :pluck

# E minor pentatonic. Five notes chosen so that any order sounds intentional.
melody = [:e4, :g4, :a4, :b4, :d5, :b4, :a4, :g4]

live_loop :tune do
  melody.each do |n|
    play n, release: 0.4
    sleep 0.25          # sixteenth notes at this tempo
  end
end

live_loop :bass do
  play :e2, release: 1.8, amp: 0.7, cutoff: 70
  sleep 2               # one bass note every two beats
end
```

Now change one thing. Set `melody` to `[:e4, :f4, :g4, :a4, :b4, :c5, :d5, :e5]`
and run it again. Same rhythm, same bass, different feeling. Working out why is
roughly what Parts 2 and 5 are for.

Press `Cmd-.` to stop it.

## Version

The examples were written against Sonic Pi 4. Later versions change defaults
occasionally, so if a snippet sounds different from its recording, check your
version before assuming you mistyped something.
